Thank you very much, Mr. President, for giving me the floor. I am delivering this statement on behalf of the African group on the recent visit of the executive board. First, the Africa group recognizes and appreciates the value in these field visits. We find real merit in field visits by the executive board because they bring the board's oversight close to realities on the ground. They allow us to move beyond documentation and understand firsthand how UN programs are being coordinated, implemented, and supported under the country conditions. Secondly, these field visits are directly linked to the mandate of the executive board. Our role is not only to approve and review, but also to monitor and understand how UN country teams are supporting member states to deliver on their priorities. We must ensure that country programming is implemented effectively and in line with the needs, commitments, and strategies of member states while also ensuring coherence among UN entities where collaboration is very important. And thirdly, Mr. President, African group underscores that field trips should lead to action, not only reflection. Fourth, Mr. President and colleagues, we believe these visits should strengthen our follow-up and learning culture, and that means ensuring that recommendations are tracked, clarifying responsibilities of implementation by the relevant actors, and reporting back to the board on what has changed and as a result of the field of the observations.
